🇲🇽🔥 HOMICIDES DOWN 49% — DAILY AVERAGE DROPS FROM 87 TO 44

García Harfuch reported today that Mexico's daily homicide average fell from 86.9 in September 2024 to 44.3 in May 2026 — a 49% reduction in 20 months.

Guanajuato alone dropped 68.5%, from 12.7 daily murders in 2018 to 4 today. Nationwide, 54,297 criminals detained, 32,000 weapons seized from organized crime.

No invasion needed. No Pentagon coalition. Just a government that governs.

🚨🇲🇽 PENTAGON CHIEF DECLARES "WAR ON CARTELS" — MEXICO CUT OUT

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told Trump's full cabinet the US is "going to war against the cartels" through the Americas Anti-Cartel Coalition — a military alliance launched in Miami that deliberately excludes Mexico.

His message to Mexico City: "Step up so we don't have to."

A country with 73.6 million drug users and record fentanyl deaths declaring hemispheric war from a cabinet room. Mexico has cut homicides 49% this administration. The Pentagon has cut nothing.

🐉🇲🇽🌐 Alibaba lands in Mexico: 400+ companies join Global E-Commerce Summit in Toluca

Chinese tech giant Alibaba held its Global E-Commerce Summit in Toluca on May 22-23, drawing over 400 Mexican companies looking to break into international digital markets. Alibaba.com Mexico director Zhang Yao told attendees: "We have the capacity to help you grow your business." The summit kicks off a nationwide tour across Mexican states.

This is what trade diversification looks like in practice. While the US threatens tariffs and demands Mexico limit its partners, China's largest e-commerce platform is on the ground training Mexican entrepreneurs to sell globally. Hugo Gómez from the State of Mexico's Development Secretariat put it plainly: "Digitalization is no longer a complementary option — it is an indispensable condition to compete."

Mexico's sovereignty isn't just about steel tariffs and oil. It's about 400 small businesses in Toluca learning to reach buyers in 190 countries — without asking Washington for permission.

🐉🇲🇽🔥 Chinese EVs head to Mexico as the US slams the door — sovereignty means options

Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa confirmed this week that the company will bring Chinese-branded Leapmotor electric vehicles to Mexico and Canada — while admitting "there is no space in the United States." Over 120 US lawmakers signed a letter demanding Trump block Chinese automakers from American soil.

Mexico doesn't need Washington's permission to build its EV future. Stellantis holds 51% of a joint venture with Leapmotor, which already sells its T03 hatchback across 13 European markets. Now the B10 electric SUV is headed to North America — through Mexico, not the US. While Trump's Congress legislates fear, Mexico opens the door to affordable clean mobility and advanced manufacturing jobs.

The contrast writes itself: the country that lectures the world about "free markets" bans competition by law. Mexico lets the market decide.

🇲🇽⚖️ "Credit rating agencies are stuck in the past — they stayed in the neoliberal era." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera May 27 Moody's methodology doesn't measure poverty reduction, welfare, or energy sovereignty. Meanwhile: record foreign investment, -49% homicides, and 76% less fentanyl reaching the US.

🇲🇽🌎 76% reduction in fentanyl reaching the US — per CBP's own data. — Claudia Sheinbaum, citing US Customs figures, mañanera May 27 The Navy: 71.4 tons of cocaine seized, 2,325 meth labs destroyed, 79,204 naval personnel deployed. The numbers are from the US government itself.

🔥🇲🇽 85 public officials detained — including 7 sitting municipal presidents. — Omar García Harfuch, Security Secretary, mañanera May 27 "This is a commitment against impunity." No protection for anyone involved in criminal activity, regardless of rank.
